title: Project V — Vulkan Engine
updateNote: Work in progress, updated after every PR.
tagline: A C++20 game engine with a hand-written Vulkan 1.3 renderer.
summary: Built from scratch as the foundation for rendering an Interstellar-style wormhole and skybox.
overview: A C++20 game engine with a hand-written Vulkan 1.3 renderer, built from scratch as the foundation for rendering an Interstellar-style wormhole and skybox.
architecture: Three modules. There's an abstract core interface (IRenderer, IWindow), an engine layer (EnTT ECS, mesh and shader managers, Assimp import), and a Vulkan backend that implements the core interface. Every Vulkan object is a move-only RAII wrapper paired with a fluent, validating builder.
highlights: FBX meshes loaded from disk and uploaded to the GPU
Pipeline cache keyed on shader pairs
ECS rotate system
Perspective camera (left-handed, Z-up)
Per-object MVP matrices sent as push constants
Frames in flight with fence and semaphore synchronisation
knownIssues: No depth buffer yet, so back faces can draw over front faces (visible in the current clip).
Vertex and index buffers are host-visible and not yet staged into device-local memory.
roadmap: Compute pipeline that ray-marches light paths through curved spacetime to render the wormhole's gravitational lensing

title: Project T
tagline: A top-down game with its own rendering pipeline for PlayStation 5 and Windows.
summary: One C++ codebase rendering through OpenGL and GLSL on Windows and the PS5 API (AGC, PSSL) on console, with deferred PBR lighting and GPU instancing.
overview: A top-down arena game built from scratch with no third-party engine. I engineered its rendering pipeline for both PlayStation 5 and Windows: OpenGL and GLSL on PC, and the PS5 rendering API (AGC) with PSSL shaders on console, behind one C++ codebase.
The game runs a timed arena level with collectibles, obstacles and a live frame-time overlay.
highlights: Cross-platform rendering pipeline for PlayStation 5 (AGC, PSSL) and Windows (OpenGL, GLSL)
Deferred lighting added to the existing PBR system, with 64 GPU-instanced point lights and 1 directional light
Instanced repeated objects such as walls and bounce pads, cutting draw calls by 42% (550 to 315)
Graphics debugging with NVIDIA Nsight Graphics and Razor GPU

title: PBR Scene in OpenGL
tagline: A physically based, deferred rendering pipeline written from scratch.
summary: A 3D scene built from scratch in C++ and OpenGL with PBR materials, deferred shading, multiple light types, tone mapping and gamma correction.
overview: A 3D scene built from scratch in C++ and OpenGL, with a physically based rendering pipeline to raise the visual quality of the scene.

After studying the GTA V rendering pipeline write-up, I moved the renderer to deferred shading. The scene is lit by directional, spot and point lights, and Reinhard tone mapping with gamma correction produces the final image.
highlights: PBR pipeline written by hand in C++, OpenGL and GLSL
Deferred rendering, informed by a study of the GTA V rendering pipeline
Directional, spot and point lights
Reinhard tone mapping and gamma correction as post-processing
Graphics debugging with NVIDIA Nsight Graphics and RenderDoc

title: Stylized Scene in OpenGL
tagline: A real-time stylized scene with GPU instancing, culling and cel shading.
summary: MSc coursework at Newcastle University: a space scene and an instanced low-poly forest, with deferred lighting, post-processing and cel shading.

metrics.label: draw call for each instanced forest

overview: A real-time rendering project built for my MSc coursework at Newcastle University, in C++, OpenGL and GLSL. It opens on a space scene and moves to a stylized low-poly world with a forest, mountains and a building.

The code is structured with object-oriented design so each system stays modular. Forests are drawn with GPU instancing, and CPU-side frustum culling with sphere tests keeps off-screen objects out of the frame.
highlights: GPU instancing draws whole forests of trees in a single draw call
CPU frustum culling with bounding-sphere tests
Deferred rendering with specular lighting
Post-processing in GLSL: saturation, desaturation and blur
Cel shading across the scene for the stylized look
Graded 74 out of 100
